_README: §23.6 — how the timetable reads your ERP's REST API. Copy this file, point
ERP_API_FILE at it, and fill in the real paths and field names.
Nothing here is required of the ERP. It describes what the ERP ALREADY
returns: any paths, any field names, any envelope, any pagination style.
The one thing that must exist is a way to look up a school by the code the
SSO token carries — that code is the contract between the two systems.
A master with no entry under `sheets` is simply 'not configured': its card
says so and its Sync button is disabled. The other masters still work, so
an ERP that has a staff endpoint today and a sections endpoint next month
can be integrated one master at a time.
After editing, run the probe from the Sync screen. It calls every endpoint
for real and names any field whose path did not resolve, showing your own
Field paths are dotted and may index arrays: 'profile.full_name', 'data.0.id'.
A field whose path is absent is LEFT ALONE by the sync, never blanked.
_AUTH: §23.8 — how we authenticate to a secured ERP API.
The ERP's SSO token is NOT used here and cannot be: it is single-use, it
expires in minutes, and we discard it at login. What IS carried over is
the useful half — `actingUserHeader` puts the ERP user id of whoever
pressed Sync on every request, so your audit log can name them. A
scheduled run omits it, and that absence is meaningful.
THE CLIENT SECRET NEVER GOES IN THIS FILE. This file is committed;
environment is not. `clientSecretEnv` names the variable holding it.

auth._optional: audience, if your provider requires it on the grant
auth._style: 'post' (default: credentials in the form body) or 'basic' (HTTP Basic)
auth._paths: accessTokenPath / expiresInPath, if the response nests them elsewhere

school._: Turns our schools.code into the id your ERP knows the school by.

Class Sections._: A REST API usually nests what SQL would join — hence the dotted paths.

_page: Only needed if the endpoint pages. `max` is a hard stop: if lastPagePath
is misread, this is what keeps the sync from looping against your
production API until something times out.
